summary: A fast, loud dice-chucker where you push your luck rolling and re-rolling for points, energy, and attacks while whoever occupies Tokyo racks up bonus points but can't heal. Games are short, swingy, and driven by table talk and gang-up dynamics rather than deep strategy.
praised: Fast, easy to teach, great gateway/family game
Card market adds variety and replayability
Plays well with kids and non-gamers
criticised: High luck/randomness can undercut player agency
Player elimination can leave people sitting out
Ganging up on the Tokyo occupant can feel mean or kingmaker-y
Shallow long-term strategy once the novelty wears off

interaction.kind: open conflict via dice attacks and take-that ganging up on whoever is in Tokyo

scoring.why: The winner is decided by racing to 20 victory points (mostly from dice and Tokyo occupancy) or by being the last monster standing after eliminating everyone else.
